title: ~을/ㄹ 만하다 [eul/l manhada] (Worth doing)
shortExplanation: Expresses that something is worthwhile or justifiable to do or experience.
longExplanation: '~을/ㄹ 만하다' is used to say that a certain action or experience is valuable enough to be done, or 'worth it.' It implies the speaker's judgment that the effort, cost, or time involved is justified.

examples.sentence: 이 케이크는 비싸지만 맛있어서 사 먹을 만해요.
examples.romanization: I keikeuneun bissajiman masisseoseo sa meogeul manhaeyo.
examples.translation: This cake is expensive, but it's so delicious that it's worth buying.

examples.sentence: 이 영화는 상영 시간이 길지만 정말 재미있어서 볼 만해요.
examples.romanization: I yeonghwaneun sangyeong sigani giljiman jeongmal jaemiisseoseo bol manhaeyo.
examples.translation: This movie has a long running time, but it's really fun, so it's worth watching.

examples.sentence: 그 밴드 공연 티켓은 비싸지만 그들의 음악은 꼭 들어볼 만해요.
examples.romanization: Geu baendeu gongyeon tikeseun bissajiman geudeurui eumageun kkok deureobol manhaeyo.
examples.translation: The band’s concert tickets are expensive, but their music is definitely worth hearing.

examples.sentence: 이 게임은 설치하는 데 오래 걸려도 해볼 만해요.
examples.romanization: I geimeun seolchihaneun de orae geollyeodo haebol manhaeyo.
examples.translation: Even though this game takes a long time to install, it's worth trying.

title: ~을/ㄹ 수록 [eul/l surok] (The more...)
shortExplanation: Shows that as one condition increases or continues, another condition also changes proportionally.
longExplanation: '~을/ㄹ 수록 [eul/l surok]' is used to express the idea that the more the first action or state intensifies, the more the second action or state does too. It corresponds to 'the more... the more...' in English.

examples.sentence: 한국어를 많이 공부할수록 한국 문화를 더 잘 이해하게 돼요.
examples.romanization: Hangukeoreul manhi gongbuhalsurok hanguk munhwareul deo jal ihaehage dwaeyo.
examples.translation: The more you study Korean, the better you understand Korean culture.

examples.sentence: 여기에 오래 있을수록 이 도시가 점점 더 좋아져요.
examples.romanization: Yeogie orae isseulsurok i dosiga jeomjeom deo joajyeoyo.
examples.translation: The longer I stay here, the more I like this city.

examples.sentence: 매일 걸을수록 건강이 좋아져요.
examples.romanization: Maeil georeulsurok geongangi joajyeoyo.
examples.translation: The more I walk every day, the healthier I become.

examples.sentence: 커피를 많이 마실수록 잠이 덜 오는 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: Keopireul manhi masilsurok jami deol oneun geot gatayo.
examples.translation: The more coffee I drink, the less sleepy I feel.

title: ~을/ㄹ 줄 알다 [eul/l jul alda] (Know how to)
shortExplanation: Used to indicate that someone knows how to perform an action or is aware of a fact.
longExplanation: '~을/ㄹ 줄 알다 [eul/l jul alda]' often translates to 'know how to do something' or 'know that...' in English. It indicates knowledge, skill, or awareness of a particular action or fact.
formation: Verb in dictionary form + 을/ㄹ 줄 알다

examples.sentence: 저는 한글을 읽을 줄 알아서 한국 드라마를 자막 없이 볼 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun hangeureul ilgeul jul araseo hanguk deuramareul jamak eopsi bol su isseoyo.
examples.translation: I know how to read Hangul, so I can watch Korean dramas without subtitles.

examples.sentence: 아빠가 요리를 잘할 줄 알았는데 어제 저녁 준비할 때 많은 문제가 생겼어요.
examples.romanization: Appaga yorireul jalhal jul aratneunde eoje jeonyeok junbihal ttae manheun munjega saenggyeosseoyo.
examples.translation: I thought Dad knew how to cook well, but there were many problems when he made dinner last night.

examples.sentence: 저는 그녀가 한국인인 줄 알고 한국어로 말했어요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun geunyeoga hangugin-in jul algo hangugeoro malhaesseoyo.
examples.translation: I knew she was Korean, so I spoke to her in Korean.

examples.sentence: 우리 강아지는 명령을 따를 줄 알아서 아주 잘 훈련되어 있어요.
examples.romanization: Uri gangajineun myeongnyeongeul ttareul jul araseo aju jal hunryeondoeeo isseoyo.
examples.translation: Our puppy knows how to follow commands, so it's well trained.

title: ~을/ㄹ지 [eul/lji] (Whether or not)
shortExplanation: Used to express uncertainty or doubt: 'whether or not'.
longExplanation: '~을/ㄹ지 [eul/lji]' indicates the speaker is unsure about an event or outcome, similar to 'whether' or 'whether or not' in English. It often appears in indirect questions or conditional statements involving doubt or possibility.

examples.sentence: 아빠가 오늘 저녁에 집에 올지 모르겠어요.
examples.romanization: Appaga oneul jeonyeoge jibe olji moreugesseoyo.
examples.translation: I’m not sure whether Dad will come home tonight.

examples.sentence: 그녀가 내일 파티에 올지 안 올지 궁금해요.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoga naeil patie olji an olji gunggeumhaeyo.
examples.translation: I’m curious whether she’ll come to the party tomorrow or not.

examples.sentence: 날이 따뜻해질지 아직 확신이 없어요.
examples.romanization: Nari ttatteuthaejilji ajik hwaksini eopseoyo.
examples.translation: I’m not sure yet whether it’ll get warmer.

examples.sentence: 당신이 제안을 받아들일지 안 받아들일지 알 수 없어요.
examples.romanization: Dangsini jean-eul badadeurilji an badadeurilji al su eopseoyo.
examples.translation: I don’t know whether you will accept the proposal or not.

title: ~을/ㄹ지도 모르다 [eul/ljido moreuda] (Might)
shortExplanation: This is used to express uncertainty or possibility.
longExplanation: '~을/ㄹ지도 모르다 [eul/ljido moreuda]', or simply 'might' in English, is a grammar pattern used to represent the speaker's uncertainty or to express the possibility of a future event or condition. Depending on context, it can imply that something might or might not happen. The verb is conjugated according to the level of formality and respect required.

examples.sentence: 내일 비가 올지도 모르니까 우산을 가져가세요.
examples.romanization: Naeil biga oljido moreunikka usaneul gajyeogaseyo.
examples.translation: It might rain tomorrow, so take an umbrella.

examples.sentence: 그는 다음 회의에 참석할지도 모릅니다.
examples.romanization: Geuneun daeum hoeuie chamseokhaljido moreumnida.
examples.translation: He might attend the next meeting.

examples.sentence: 저는 아마 내년에 한국으로 이사할지도 몰라요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun ama naenyeon-e hangug-euro isahaljido mollayo.
examples.translation: I might move to Korea next year.

examples.sentence: 그녀가 그 소식을 알고 있을지도 모르죠.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoga geu sosigeul algo isseuljido moreujyo.
examples.translation: She might know that news.

title: ~을/ㄹ지라도 [eul/ljirado] (Even if)
shortExplanation: Used to say 'even if'; 'no matter how/if'; nonetheless.
longExplanation: '~을/ㄹ지라도 [eul/ljirado]' is a conditional form used in Korean to express the meaning of 'even if', 'no matter how', or 'nonetheless'. It indicates that the expected result will remain unchanged regardless of the given condition.

examples.sentence: 문제가 어렵지라도 포기하지 않고 계속 풀어볼게요.
examples.romanization: Munjega eoryeobjirado pogihaji anhgo gyesok pulleobolgeyo.
examples.translation: Even if the problem is difficult, I won't give up and I'll keep trying to solve it.

examples.sentence: 비가 오지라도 갈 생각이에요, 제가 중요한 미팅이 있어요.
examples.romanization: Biga ojirado gal saenggakieyo, jaega jungyohan mitingi isseoyo.
examples.translation: Even if it's raining, I'm planning to go because I have an important meeting.

examples.sentence: 버스가 빨리 오지라도, 무리해서 뛰지 않을 거예요.
examples.romanization: Beoseuga pparei ojirado, murihaseo ttwiji aneul geoyeyo.
examples.translation: Even if the bus comes quickly, I won't run excessively.

examples.sentence: 비용이 많이 들지라도 좋은 품질의 제품을 만들고 싶어요.
examples.romanization: Biyongi manhi deuljirado joheun pumjilui jepumeul mandeulgo sippeoyo.
examples.translation: Even if it costs a lot, I want to make a product of good quality.

title: ~을/ㄹ지 몰라 [eul/lji molla] (Maybe)
shortExplanation: Used to express uncertainty or doubt; 'maybe', 'might', 'I don't know if'.
longExplanation: '~을/ㄹ지 몰라 [eul/lji molla]' is a grammar form used to indicate doubts, uncertainties, or suppositions. It can be translated as 'maybe', 'might', or 'I don’t know if' in English. This form is typically used when the speaker is unsure of something or wishes to present a speculative premise.

examples.sentence: 그녀가 내일 학교에 올지 몰라, 요즘 아프다니까.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoga naeil haggyoe olji molla, yojeum apeudanikka.
examples.translation: Maybe she will come to school tomorrow; she said she's been sick lately.

examples.sentence: 이 물건을 사려고 했는데, 아직 돈이 충분할지 몰라요.
examples.romanization: I mulgeoneul saryeogo haetneunde, ajik doni chungbunhalji mollayo.
examples.translation: I was planning to buy this item, but I don't know if I have enough money.

examples.sentence: 내일 비가 올지 몰라서 우산을 준비해야겠어요.
examples.romanization: Naeil biga olji mollaseo usaneul junbihaeyagesseoyo.
examples.translation: I should prepare an umbrella because it might rain tomorrow.

examples.sentence: 어떤 옷을 입을지 몰라서 세 가지를 준비했어요.
examples.romanization: Eoddeon oseul ibeulji mollaseo se gajireul junbihaesseoyo.
examples.translation: I prepared three different options because I'm not sure which clothes to wear.

title: ~을래요 [eullaeyo] (Want to)
shortExplanation: Used to express the speaker's desire or intention to do something.
longExplanation: '~을래요 [eullaeyo]' is a verb ending used in Korean to express an intention, suggestion, or polite proposal from the speaker's perspective. It denotes that the speaker wants or would like to do something and is often used when making plans or suggestions. Note that it is typically used for the speaker’s own actions.

examples.sentence: 저는 오늘 집에서 영화를 볼래요, 밖으로 나가기는 너무 추워요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun oneul jibeseo yeonghwareul bollae, bakkeuro nagagineun neomu chuwoyo.
examples.translation: I want to watch a movie at home today because it's too cold to go out.

examples.sentence: 우리 이번 주말에 캠핑장에 가서 텐트를 칠래요, 어떻게 생각해요?
examples.romanization: Uri ibeon jumal-e keampingjang-e gaseo tent-eul chillae, eotteoke saengkaekhae?
examples.translation: How about we go to the campground this weekend and pitch a tent?

examples.sentence: 나는 저녁으로 한 끼만 먹을래요, 이미 배가 불러서 더 먹지 않을래요.
examples.romanization: Naneun jeonyeoge han kkiman meogeullae, imi baega bulleoseo deo meokji anheullae.
examples.translation: I want to have just one meal for dinner because I'm already full and don't want to eat more.

examples.sentence: 나는 이번 주말에 연극 보러 갈래요, 한국 문화를 좋아해서 결심했어요.
examples.romanization: Naneun ibeon jumal-e yeongeuk boreo gallae, hanguk munhwareul joahaseo gyeolsimhaesseoyo.
examples.translation: I've decided to go see a play this weekend because I like Korean culture.

title: ~을 리가 없다 [eulliga eopda] (It's unlikely that)
shortExplanation: This expression is used to indicate that a certain situation is unlikely or impossible to happen.
longExplanation: '~을 리가 없다 [eulliga eopda]' is a speculative expression used in Korean to indicate that something is improbable or implausible based on the speaker's judgment. It expresses disbelief or doubt about the possibility of an event occurring and is often used to contrast a hypothetical situation with reality.

examples.sentence: 이것이 사실일 리가 없어요, 그가 그런 일을 저지를 사람이 아니에요.
examples.romanization: Igeosi sasilliga eobs-eoyo, geuga geuleon il-eul jeojileul salam-i ani-eyo.
examples.translation: It's unlikely that this is true; he's not the type of person to do such a thing.

examples.sentence: 그녀가 날 잊어버릴 리가 없어요, 우리 너무 오래 같이 지냈거든요.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoga nal ijeobeoriliga eobs-eoyo, uli neomu olae gati jinaessgeodeunyo.
examples.translation: It's unlikely that she would forget me; we've been together for so long.

examples.sentence: 저는 이 계약서를 사인할 리가 없어요, 제가 아직 조건들을 모두 이해하지 못했어요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun i gyeagseoreul sainhal liga eobseoyo, jega ajik jogeondeul-eul modu ihaehaji moshaesseoyo.
examples.translation: It's unlikely that I will sign this contract because I still do not fully understand the terms.

examples.sentence: 그가 오늘 올 리가 없어요, 그거 알고 있어요, 그가 아픈 걸.
examples.romanization: Geuga oneul ol riga eopseoyo, geugeo algo isseoyo, geuga apeun geol.
examples.translation: It's unlikely that he will come today; everyone knows that he's sick.

title: ~을수록 [eulsurok] (The more)
shortExplanation: Used to express 'the more...the more', indicating an increasing degree or intensity.
longExplanation: The grammar point '~을수록 [eulsurok]' is used in Korean to indicate that as one condition intensifies, another condition increases proportionately. It is equivalent to the English phrase 'the more...the more', showing a direct proportional relationship between two events or states.

examples.sentence: 한국어를 공부할수록, 한국 문화에 대해 더 많이 이해할 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: Hanguk-eoreul gongbu halsurok, hanguk munhwa-e daehae deo mani ihaehal su isseoyo.
examples.translation: The more I study Korean, the more I can understand Korean culture.

examples.sentence: 이 노래를 많이 들을수록, 더 좋아지는 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: I noraereul mani deureulsurok, deo joajineun geot gatayo.
examples.translation: The more I listen to this song, the more I seem to like it.

examples.sentence: 날이 점점 더워질수록, 아이스크림이 더 많이 팔려요.
examples.romanization: Nal-i jeomjeom deoweojilsurok, aiseukeurimi deo manhi pallyeoyo.
examples.translation: The hotter the day gets, the more ice cream is sold.

examples.sentence: 사람들이 친환경 제품을 사용할수록, 환경보호에 더 많은 기여를 할 수 있습니다.
examples.romanization: Saramdeuri chinhwangyeong jepumeul sayonghalsurok, hwangyeong bohoe deo manheun giyeoreul hal su itsseumnida.
examples.translation: The more people use eco-friendly products, the more they can contribute to environmental protection.

title: ~을지언정 [euljieonjeong] (Even though)
shortExplanation: This phrase is used to indicate 'even though' or 'despite'.
longExplanation: '~을지언정 [euljieonjeong]' is a conjunction in Korean that conveys the meaning of 'even though', 'even if', or 'despite'. It is used to present a contrasting situation or fact that exists despite the previous condition. While more common in formal or written language, it is also useful in everyday contexts and for tests like TOPIK.

examples.sentence: 그것이 그에게 굉장히 중요한 일일지언정, 그는 결코 그것에 손을 대지 않았다.
examples.romanization: Geugeosi geuege goengjanghi jungyohan iriljieonjeong, geuneun gyeolko geugeos-e son-eul daeji anh-assda.
examples.translation: Even though that was very important to him, he never laid a hand on it.

examples.sentence: 그가 부자일지언정, 평소에 아주 절약하는 습관이 있다.
examples.romanization: Geuga bujailjieonjeong, pyeongso-e aju jeolyaghamyeon seubgwan-i issda.
examples.translation: Even though he is rich, he has a habit of being very thrifty.

examples.sentence: 시험이 어려울지언정, 학생들은 열심히 공부했어요.
examples.romanization: Siheom-i eoryeouljieonjeong, haksaengdeureun yeolshimhi gongbuhaesseoyo.
examples.translation: Even though the exam was difficult, the students studied hard.

examples.sentence: 그 공원이 아름다울지언정, 저녁에는 위험이 많으니 조심하세요.
examples.romanization: Geu gong-woni aleumdauljieonjeong, jeonyeogeneun wihemi manh-euni joshimhaseyo.
examples.translation: Even though that park is beautiful, it becomes dangerous in the evening, so be careful.

title: ~이나 [ina] (Or, whether)
shortExplanation: Used to indicate choice or alternatives, typically attached to nouns.
longExplanation: '~이나 [ina]' is a particle in Korean attached to nouns to indicate alternatives or choices. It functions similarly to 'or' in English and is used to present different options or possibilities. The proper formation is with a noun followed by (이)나.

examples.sentence: 사과나 오렌지, 그 중 하나만 골라주세요.
examples.romanization: Sagwana orenji, geu jung hanaman gollajuseyo.
examples.translation: Please choose either an apple or an orange.

examples.sentence: 영화나 드라마를 볼까요?
examples.romanization: Yeonghwa na deuramareul bolkkayo?
examples.translation: Shall we watch a movie or a drama?

examples.sentence: 버스나 택시를 타세요.
examples.romanization: Beoseu na taegsi-reul taseyo.
examples.translation: Take either a bus or a taxi.

title: ~이든 [ideun] (Either or)
shortExplanation: Used to present two or more choices; 'either', 'or'.
longExplanation: '~이든 [ideun]' is a connecting ending used in Korean to present two or more alternatives or choices. It is analogous to 'either' or 'or' in English and is commonly used when the speaker considers all options equally acceptable.

examples.sentence: 피자든 파스타든 무엇을 먹어도 좋아요, 둘 다 맛있으니까요.
examples.romanization: Pijadeun pasteudeun mueoseul meogeodo joayo, dul da masisseunikka yo.
examples.translation: Whether it's pizza or pasta, either is fine because both are delicious.

examples.sentence: 운동이든 요가든 모든 활동이 건강에 좋아요.
examples.romanization: Undongideun yogadeun modeun hwaldongi geongang-e joayo.
examples.translation: Whether it’s exercise or yoga, all activities are good for your health.

examples.sentence: 친구들하고 영화보기이든, 책을 읽는 것이든 저는 행복해요.
examples.romanization: Chingudeulhago yeonghwabogideun, chaeg-eul ilgneun geosideun jeoneun haengbokhaeyo.
examples.translation: Whether it's watching movies with friends or reading a book, I am happy.

examples.sentence: 떡볶이이든, 부대찌개든 저는 둘 다 좋아하는 음식입니다.
examples.romanization: Tteokbokkiideun, budaejjigaedeun jeoneun dul da joahaneun eumsigibnida.
examples.translation: Whether it's tteokbokki or budae jjigae, I like both foods.

title: ~이라도 [irado] (At least, even if)
shortExplanation: Used to express 'at least' or 'even if'; refers to a minimum or lesser expectation.
longExplanation: The '~이라도 [irado]' grammar point is used in Korean to express a minimum expectation or to settle for a lesser alternative when the preferred option isn’t available. It conveys the idea of conceding to a less ideal scenario and is often used when faced with challenges or limited choices.

examples.sentence: 이 작은 선물이라도 받아주세요. 저는 더 좋은 선물을 줄 수 없어요.
examples.romanization: I jageun seonmurirado badajuseyo. Jeoneun deo joheun seonmureul jul su eobseoyo.
examples.translation: Please accept this small gift at least. I can’t give a better gift.

examples.sentence: 미안하다고 말이라도 해 줬으면 좋겠어요.
examples.romanization: Mianhadago marirado hae jwosseumyeon johgesseoyo.
examples.translation: I wish you would at least say you’re sorry.

examples.sentence: 비록 그녀가 나를 싫어한다고 해도, 친구로서라도 계속 만나고 싶어요.
examples.romanization: Birok geunyeoga nareul sirheohanda고 haedo, chinguroseorado gyesok mannago sippeoyo.
examples.translation: Even if she dislikes me, I want to keep seeing her, at least as friends.

examples.sentence: 신발은 원하는 색깔이 없으니까, 흰색이라도 사겠어요.
examples.romanization: Sinbal-eun wonhaneun saekkkal-i eobseunikka, huinsaekirado sa gesseoyo.
examples.translation: Since the shoes don’t come in the color I want, I’ll buy the white ones at least.

title: ~이라는 것 [iraneun geot] (The thing called)
shortExplanation: This phrase is used to refer to or define something that was mentioned earlier.
longExplanation: '~이라는 것 [iraneun geot]' is a sentence structure used in Korean to refer to or define a particular thing or idea. It is often used in explanations to elaborate on a concept or to highlight specific characteristics.

examples.sentence: 사랑이라는 것이 어떤 것인지, 많은 사람들이 꼭 알고 싶어 하는 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: Sarangiraneun geosi eotteon geotinji, maneun saramdeul-i kkok algo sip-eo haneun geot gatayo.
examples.translation: It seems like many people really want to know what this thing called love is.

examples.sentence: 성공이라는 것은 많은 노력과 헌신 없이는 이루어질 수 없는 것입니다.
examples.romanization: Seonggongiraneun geoseun maneun noryeokgwa heonsin eobsineun irueojil su eobseun geosibnida.
examples.translation: Success cannot be achieved without a lot of effort and dedication.

examples.sentence: 행복이라는 것은 개인마다 다른 의미를 갖고 있기 때문에 정의하기가 어렵습니다.
examples.romanization: Haengbogiraneun geoseun gaenmada dareun uimireul gajgo issgie ttaemune jeonguihagiga eoryeopseumnida.
examples.translation: It’s difficult to define happiness because it holds different meanings for each person.
